report_metadata.sdlc_rationale: Requirements fully defined and signed off, team has direct experience with React/Python/Django stack, fixed 3-month deadline with no flexibility signals, changes mid-project not expected.

project_understanding.primary_goal: Add real-time reporting and alerting capabilities to the existing customer analytics dashboard to eliminate manual report generation.
project_understanding.beneficiary: Customer success team (15 people) and Sales team (25 people)
project_understanding.trigger: CSMs spending 10 hours/week on manual report generation; leadership mandate to automate dashboards and reduce manual effort.
success_definition: CSMs can create custom reports in < 5 minutes
90% of scheduled reports delivered on time
supporting_quotes: Customer success managers are spending 10 hours/week manually generating reports
Add real-time reporting and alerting capabilities to our existing customer analytics dashboard

hard_constraints.compliance: SSO integration required; data retention 2 years

non_functional_requirements.usability: Custom reports creatable in < 5 minutes (usability target)
non_functional_requirements.scalability: Support 40 concurrent users (15 CSMs + 25 sales, peak usage)

assumption_log.what: Team composition: 3 developers assumed to be 1 frontend, 1 backend, 1 full-stack or QA-capable; no QA engineer explicitly named.
assumption_log.why: Standard internal tool enhancement team structure; QA responsibilities distributed across developers on small teams is common for internal projects.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 9.2 — Resource estimation tied to WBS; team composition inferred from project scope.
assumption_log.consequence: If developers cannot allocate 25% of effort to QA (PMBOK 8.2 minimum), test coverage will be insufficient and bugs will reach production.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows planning with stated team size. Risks: if actual team lacks QA discipline, critical bugs in alerting logic could cause SLA failures (alert response time > 1 hour).

assumption_log.what: Budget is not constrained; project is assumed to proceed within standard internal tool allocation (no external vendors, no infrastructure overages).
assumption_log.why: Internal enhancement project using existing stack (React, Django, PostgreSQL, PagerDuty); no new platform or licensing mentioned.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 7.1 — Cost baseline derived from resource plan; internal projects typically have implicit budget approval.
assumption_log.consequence: If budget is actually constrained (e.g., hiring freeze, infrastructure costs), timeline will slip or scope will be cut.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows planning to proceed without budget re-negotiation. Risks: if budget is actually limited, scope reduction or timeline extension required mid-project.

assumption_log.what: Existing dashboard codebase is maintainable and well-documented; no major technical debt blocking new feature integration.
assumption_log.why: Input describes 'existing customer analytics dashboard' as the base; enhancement projects assume the foundation is sound unless stated otherwise.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.2 — Scope baseline assumes existing system is stable; technical debt is a risk, not a baseline assumption.
assumption_log.consequence: If codebase has significant technical debt, refactoring will consume 20-30% of Phase 2 effort, compressing feature delivery and risking deadline miss.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows Phase 2 to focus on new features immediately. Risks: if codebase is brittle, integration of real-time refresh and alerting will be slower and riskier.

assumption_log.what: PagerDuty integration is straightforward (API-based, no custom webhook development required); PagerDuty sandbox/test environment is available.
assumption_log.why: PagerDuty is a mature SaaS platform with standard REST API; integration complexity is typically low for alert routing.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 11.2 — Risk identification; external API dependencies are flagged as integration risks.
assumption_log.consequence: If PagerDuty API is more complex than expected or sandbox access is delayed, Phase 3 integration testing will slip by 1-2 weeks.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: allows Phase 3 to proceed with standard integration effort. Risks: if PagerDuty integration requires custom webhook logic or API rate limiting is restrictive, effort increases.

critical_path_summary.staffing_implication: Backend developer and frontend developer must be full-time on critical path; PM must coordinate across all phases; any part-time allocation will compress timeline.

phases.name: Discovery & Design
milestones: Requirements document finalized and signed off

tasks.name: Audit existing dashboard codebase and identify integration points
tasks.definition_of_done: Technical audit document completed identifying all existing APIs, data models, and integration points for real-time refresh and alerting.

tasks.name: Define custom report schema and filtering requirements
tasks.definition_of_done: Report schema document approved by customer success team lead; filtering logic requirements documented.

tasks.name: Design real-time data refresh architecture and alerting workflow
tasks.definition_of_done: Architecture diagram approved by tech lead; data refresh interval (15 min), alert routing logic, and PagerDuty integration points documented.

tasks.name: Design UI mockups for custom report builder and alert configuration
tasks.definition_of_done: Figma mockups completed and approved by customer success team; accessibility checklist (WCAG 2.1 AA) verified.

phases.name: Core Development
milestones: Custom report builder core features working

tasks.name: Implement real-time data refresh pipeline (15-minute interval)
tasks.definition_of_done: Data refresh runs every 15 minutes; latency < 2 seconds; no data loss on refresh; monitoring logs all refresh events.

tasks.name: Build custom report builder UI (date range, filtering, widget selection)
tasks.definition_of_done: Report builder allows custom date range, KPI widget selection, and filtering in < 5 minutes; UI tested with 3 CSM representatives.

tasks.name: Implement email scheduling service and PDF/CSV export
tasks.definition_of_done: Email scheduling works; PDF and CSV exports generated correctly; scheduled reports sent on time; delivery logs captured.

tasks.name: Implement KPI dashboard widgets and real-time data binding
tasks.definition_of_done: Widgets display real-time data; refresh every 15 minutes; no stale data displayed; performance acceptable on 40 concurrent users.

tasks.name: Integrate PagerDuty alerting and test alert routing
tasks.definition_of_done: Alerts route to PagerDuty correctly; alert response time < 1 hour verified in test; escalation policies tested; no alert loss.

tasks.name: Verify SSO authentication integration and session management
tasks.definition_of_done: SSO login works; session timeout enforced; user roles and permissions respected; no authentication bypass.

tasks.name: Implement data retention policy (2-year archival and deletion)
tasks.definition_of_done: Data older than 2 years automatically archived; deletion job runs monthly; audit log captures all deletions; compliance verified.

tasks.name: Test edge cases: null data, missing KPIs, concurrent report generation
tasks.definition_of_done: All edge cases handled gracefully; error messages clear; no UI crashes; concurrent report generation tested with 10 simultaneous requests.

phases.name: QA & Testing
milestones: UAT completed with customer success team

tasks.name: Execute regression test suite on existing dashboard features
tasks.definition_of_done: All existing dashboard features tested; no regressions found; test results documented.

tasks.name: Conduct UAT with customer success team (5 CSMs, 2 sales reps)
tasks.definition_of_done: UAT sign-off from CSM lead; all success criteria validated (< 5 min report creation, 90% on-time delivery, < 1 hour alert response); feedback documented.

tasks.name: Performance testing: 40 concurrent users, 15-min refresh, alert latency
tasks.definition_of_done: Load test passes with 40 concurrent users; refresh latency < 2 sec; alert delivery < 1 hour; no timeouts or errors.

tasks.name: Security review and penetration testing (internal)
tasks.definition_of_done: Security review completed; no critical vulnerabilities found; SSO and data access controls verified; audit trail functional.

tasks.name: Deploy to production and verify all features working
tasks.definition_of_done: All features deployed; smoke tests pass; no errors in production logs; rollback plan tested.

tasks.name: Configure monitoring, alerting, and operational dashboards
tasks.definition_of_done: Monitoring dashboards show system health; alerts configured for failures; on-call runbook updated.

tasks.name: Write user documentation, training materials, and handoff to support
tasks.definition_of_done: User guide completed; training video recorded; support team trained; go-live sign-off from CSM lead.

risk_register.description: If existing dashboard codebase has significant technical debt or poor documentation, integration of real-time refresh and alerting will require refactoring, consuming 20-30% of Phase 2 effort and risking deadline miss.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 1 audit reveals complex or brittle code; developers report integration complexity higher than expected.
risk_register.mitigation: Complete thorough codebase audit in Phase 1 (T1); identify refactoring needs before Phase 2 starts; allocate 10% buffer in Phase 2 for unexpected technical debt.
risk_register.contingency: If refactoring is required, defer non-critical features (e.g., advanced filtering) to Phase 2 post-launch; extend timeline by 1 week if necessary.

risk_register.description: If PagerDuty API integration is more complex than expected (custom webhook logic, rate limiting, schema mismatches), Phase 3 integration testing will slip by 1-2 weeks.
risk_register.trigger: PagerDuty API documentation reveals unexpected complexity; sandbox testing shows integration issues; rate limiting is more restrictive than assumed.
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm PagerDuty sandbox access and API documentation in Phase 1; spike on PagerDuty integration in early Phase 2 (T5) before full implementation; test alert routing in Phase 3 early.
risk_register.contingency: If integration is blocked, implement simplified alerting (email-only) as fallback; defer PagerDuty integration to Phase 2 post-launch.

risk_register.description: If the 3-developer team is pulled to other projects or any developer becomes unavailable, critical path tasks (real-time refresh, alerting, email scheduling) will slip immediately.
risk_register.trigger: Developer assigned to competing project; developer illness or departure; unplanned context switching.
risk_register.mitigation: Secure written commitment from engineering leadership that 3 developers are full-time on this project for 12 weeks; establish clear escalation path if capacity is threatened; cross-train developers on critical components.
risk_register.contingency: If a developer becomes unavailable, immediately escalate to engineering leadership; reduce scope (defer non-critical features) or extend timeline by 2-3 weeks.

risk_register.description: If Phase 1 requirements gathering or architecture design takes longer than 1.7 weeks, downstream phases will compress and critical path tasks will be at risk.
risk_register.trigger: Stakeholder alignment takes multiple iterations; architecture decisions delayed; codebase audit reveals unexpected complexity.
risk_register.mitigation: Schedule Phase 1 kickoff immediately; set hard deadline for requirements sign-off (end of week 1); use architecture spike (T3) to validate design early.
risk_register.contingency: If Phase 1 slips, compress Phase 2 by deferring non-critical features (e.g., advanced filtering) to post-launch; extend overall timeline by 1 week.

risk_register.description: If customer success team requests additional features during development (e.g., advanced filtering, custom KPI calculations), scope creep will consume Phase 2 effort and delay delivery.
risk_register.trigger: Stakeholder requests new features during Phase 2 or Phase 3; 'nice to have' features are treated as must-haves; scope change requests submitted without formal change control.
risk_register.mitigation: Establish formal change control process in Phase 1; document MVP scope clearly; schedule weekly stakeholder sync to manage expectations; use feature flags to defer non-critical features.
risk_register.contingency: If scope creep occurs, formally document change request; assess impact on timeline; defer feature to Phase 2 post-launch or extend deadline by 1-2 weeks.

risk_register.description: If data retention policy (2-year archival) is not implemented correctly, compliance audit could fail and require rework post-launch.
risk_register.trigger: Data retention job fails silently; audit log does not capture deletions; compliance review identifies gaps.
risk_register.mitigation: Implement data retention policy in Phase 3 (T11) with automated testing; verify audit logs capture all deletions; conduct compliance review before Phase 5 deployment.
risk_register.contingency: If compliance issues are found post-launch, implement corrective action immediately; conduct full data audit to ensure no violations.

risk_register.description: If real-time data refresh (15-minute interval) causes database performance degradation, alert delivery and report generation will be slow, missing the < 1 hour alert response SLA.
risk_register.trigger: Performance testing (T15) shows refresh latency > 2 seconds; database CPU spikes during refresh; alert delivery delayed.
risk_register.mitigation: Design refresh pipeline with query optimization and caching in Phase 1 (T3); implement incremental refresh (only changed data) in Phase 2 (T5); conduct performance testing early in Phase 4 (T15).
risk_register.contingency: If performance issues occur, implement database indexing or query optimization; increase refresh interval to 30 minutes if necessary; defer advanced filtering to post-launch.

risk_register.description: If QA effort is not allocated at minimum 25% of development effort (PMBOK 8.2), test coverage will be insufficient and critical bugs will reach production.
risk_register.trigger: Developers allocate < 25% effort to testing; Phase 4 QA timeline is compressed; critical bugs found post-launch.
risk_register.mitigation: Allocate 25% of developer effort to QA (Phase 3-4); establish automated test suite in Phase 2; conduct regression testing in Phase 4 (T13); require UAT sign-off before deployment.
risk_register.contingency: If bugs are found post-launch, implement hotfix process; extend Phase 4 by 1 week if necessary to increase test coverage.

staffing_plan.notes: Full-time PM oversight across all phases; responsible for stakeholder alignment, change control, and UAT coordination. Allocation is 12% of total project hours (within 10-15% PMBOK 9.2 range).
Full-time on critical path; owns real-time refresh pipeline (T5), email scheduling (T7), PagerDuty integration (T9), data retention (T11), and performance testing (T15). No part-time allocation.
Full-time on Phases 2-4; owns report builder UI (T6), KPI widgets (T8), edge case testing (T12), and regression testing (T13). Has 1-2 days slack on non-critical tasks.

Assumed from shared QA pool (not explicitly named in input); allocated 14% of total hours, meeting PMBOK 8.2 minimum of 25% of dev effort (180h dev × 25% = 45h; 70h QA > 45h minimum). Responsible for regression testing (T13), UAT coordination (T14), and performance testing (T15).

open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If sandbox access is delayed or API is more complex than expected, Phase 3 integration testing (T9) will slip by 1-2 weeks.
